interactions.summary: A student says Dante helps by writing the book, and Jiang confirms that this is the necessary form the message must take.

Jiang asks what humans have that God lacks, hears partial student answers about time, ignorance, and rational tools, then lands on imagination as the decisive human faculty that makes Divine Comedy possible.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang leading students toward his conclusion

speaker_notes.note: The student sentence is cut off by interruption, but the intended point is that humans can imagine because they do not already know everything.

claims.claim: A student answers that Dante can help others on the journey by writing Divine Comedy as a book.
Jiang says the reason Dante had to undergo the heavenly journey is so he could write Divine Comedy and help readers take the journey themselves.
Students offer partial answers that human beings possess a concept of space and time and the condition of not already knowing everything.
A student suggests Dante used logic and rationalism, even though those are among the things he was trying to preach against.
Jiang's answer is that the distinctively human faculty is imagination, which perfection excludes because a being that already knows everything cannot fail or imagine.
Jiang says Beatrice cannot communicate directly with our world because she lacks the imagination to do so, and Dante must translate divine truth into imaginative human form by writing the poem.
Jiang characterizes Dante as 'basically a journalist' invited to heaven to do reporting and then write it beautifully for everyone else.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang makes imagination the missing divine faculty and the exact thing that lets Dante turn heaven into literature.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the lecture's core mechanism for why revelation requires a human poet rather than a perfect heavenly being.

signature_moments.moment: Dante becomes a journalist who reports from heaven for the rest of us.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The metaphor compresses Jiang's entire account of why the poem exists and how it mediates divine truth to ordinary readers.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's name for the human power unavailable to perfection and therefore necessary for writing Divine Comedy.
Jiang's metaphor for Dante as a reporter sent to heaven who must bring back a written account for others.

chronology_notes.note: The packet converts the free-will explanation into a transmission mechanism: Dante's journey matters because it is later rewritten through imagination into a book that readers can inhabit for themselves.
